section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the statistical analyses used: descriptive statistics and Pearson product-moment correlations were computed to examine associations among age, BMI, early memories of warmth and safeness (EMWSS, EMWSS_peers), social safeness (SSPS), body appreciation (BAS-2), and eating psychopathology (EDE-Q). Path analyses (using AMOS and Maximum Likelihood estimation) tested a mediation model with EMWSS variables as exogenous predictors, SSPS and BAS-2 as mediators, and EDE-Q as outcome, with bootstrap resampling (5000 samples) for indirect effects and multiple fit indices reported.
section_summary.evidence_source: Data analyses were performed using the software IBM SPSS Statistics 22.0 (SPSS  IBM; Chicago, IL) and path analyses with the software AMOS (Arbuckle, 2008). Additionally, to explore the associations between age, BMI, early memories of warmth and safeness with close figures (EMWSS) and with peers (EMWSS_peers), social safeness (SSPS), body appreciation (BAS-2) and eating psychopathology (EDE-Q), product-moment Pearson correlations analyses were performed. Finally, path analyses were conducted to estimate the presumed relations within the proposed model (Figure 1)... The Maximum Likelihood method was used... Bootstrap resampling method, with 5000 Bootstrap samples, and 95% bias-corrected confidence intervals around the standardized estimated of total, direct and indirect effects.
